components.text: The biblical identification must discriminate Christian testimony from comparably confident rival religious revelation claims.
Whether confidence in Christian testimony discriminates biblical revelation from comparably confident rival religious claims.
Open inquiry requires a method that distinguishes evidentially supported nonmaterial claims from insulated assertions.
Whether openness to nonmaterial conclusions still requires observable consequences that distinguish a claim from nonexistence.
The causal regress must justify terminating in God rather than an unknown terminus or an uncaused universe.
Whether the causal regress justifies stopping at God and identifies the terminus as supernatural rather than unknown or uncaused.
Human fallibility does not by itself establish that every proposition must receive only intermediate probabilistic confidence.
Whether fallibility and probabilistic discipline rule out justified certainty about any burden-relevant foundational proposition.
Religious disagreement and rival confidence require a truth-discriminating comparison rather than an appeal to consensus.
Whether religious disagreement and rival inspired scriptures prevent Christianity from being evidentially distinguished as true.
The claim that objective morality requires God must confront a secular standard grounded in sentient flourishing and suffering.
Whether objective moral judgment requires a personal divine source rather than facts about sentient suffering and flourishing.
The moral significance of suffering does not entail that every permitted instance is incompatible with divine goodness.
Whether sentient well-being can ground objective morality without a personal divine source.
A general appeal to mysterious or redemptive purpose must explain why an omnipotent God permits devastating innocent natural suffering.
Whether a possible redemptive pattern adequately reconciles devastating innocent suffering with omnipotence and benevolence.
The claim that morality requires God must address an evolutionary account of cooperative dispositions and internalized virtue.
Whether moral behavior and objective-seeming standards require divine command rather than evolved social capacities.
An evolutionary explanation of cooperation must establish objective authority rather than only adaptive self-interest and social behavior.
A flourishing standard must explain why its values are objectively binding rather than selected preferences.
Whether evolved cooperation explains objectively binding moral standards or only adaptive self-interest and social behavior.
Whether well-being and flourishing supply objective authority rather than selected human values.
The reported resurrection must be supported strongly enough to discriminate it from comparable testimony and ordinary error.
Comparative religious evaluation must apply the same evidential standard to rival miracle and revival claims.
Whether testimony and extraordinary character provide sufficiently discriminating historical support for resurrection and divine identity.
Apparently unfair earthly suffering may be ultimately rectified if persons receive an eternal afterlife and redemptive outcome.
Whether severe innocent suffering remains gratuitous if it can transform persons and be fully rectified in an eternal afterlife.
Apparent biological design must discriminate top-down intelligence from bottom-up natural selection producing functional adaptations.
The broader denial of natural explanatory capacity does not answer the observable biological mechanism.
Afterlife rectification is unrelated to the biological design inference addressed here.
Whether functional biological organization requires top-down intelligence when an observable bottom-up mechanism produces adaptation.
Fine-tuning must warrant design despite unresolved physics rather than merely occupy a current explanatory gap.
Whether unresolved values of physical constants constitute positive evidence requiring an intelligent designer.
If physical matter cannot cause its own total existence, the required terminus must lie beyond physical matter.
Unresolved fine-tuning physics is not the causal-regress issue addressed by this reply.
Whether an epistemic regress boundary can be identified as nonphysical because physical matter cannot cause its own total existence.
Natural selection must explain the origin of complex functional information and integrated structures, not merely label them functional.
Unresolved physical fine-tuning is separate from the biological information argument made here.
Whether natural selection adequately explains the origin of complex functional information and integrated biological systems.
Whether incomplete physics defeats the separate inference from fine-tuned constants to intelligence.
